content:
Ibrahim Khan: Kicking off coordination on the canonical examples refresh. We need to align on naming + event semantics before folks update SDK snippets.

Main question: do we call it “function calling” (older docs + some SDK naming) or “tool calling” (more recent product + API terminology)?

Also: where is the single source of truth going to live (docs repo vs examples repo)?

Monica Patel: +1 to picking *one* term and sticking to it across Python/TS/Go + docs-site. Support volume is spiking because users copy/paste different snippets that disagree. 

My preference: user-facing “tool calling” but we can note “functions” in one sentence for migration.

Dana Lo: In TS land we currently expose `tools: [...]` in the client examples, but a bunch of README text still says “function calling”. I can update either way, but it needs to match docs-site + product copy.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go SDK has a couple places that say “function” because we modeled it after OpenAI-ish wording early on. Renaming in code is a bigger lift, but *examples/docs* can definitely say “tools” and treat “function” as the old alias.

Elliot Price: From docs POV, I want to avoid “function calling” because it reads like “execute arbitrary code” to some readers. “Tools” is clearer and we can add a safety callout (“you control the tool implementation”).

Henry Cho: Product is leaning “tool calling” everywhere user-facing. Also structured outputs: we should not call it “JSON mode” in docs anymore; call it “structured output” and lead with schema.

Brian Murphy: API side: the wire format is `tool_calls` in the streamed deltas and final response, so docs saying “function calls” is already inconsistent. We still accept legacy params in a couple places for compat, but canonical needs to match the response.

Amara Diallo: Gateway emits `tool_call.delta` events + `tool_call.completed` (depending on SDK wrapper) and then the final response object has `tool_calls`. If docs say “function_call”, users will look for the wrong key and file bugs.

Sabrina James: On the “source of truth”: can we centralize in `redwood-examples` repo and have docs-site + SDK READMEs link there? Otherwise we’ll keep drifting.

Monica Patel: That’s the direction. Canonical examples live in redwood-examples, then:
- docs-site uses the same code blocks (copy/paste or pulled via snippet sync)
- SDK repos link to canonical examples and only keep minimal quick snippets
- CI snippet tests run against the canonical folder

Ibrahim Khan: +1. I’ll write that into the internal canonical patterns doc + parity matrix.

Proposed wording:
- “Tool calling” is the primary term.
- First mention: “Tool calling (sometimes called function calling in older examples) lets the model request you run *tools* you define.”
- In code: use `tools` / `tool_calls` consistently.

Dana Lo: Works for TS.

Mateusz Zielinski: Works for Go.

Elliot Price: Works for docs. Please also add a glossary note so searchers for “function calling” land on the tool calling page.

Marcus Lin: Security nit: if we’re standardizing terminology, also standardize the safe pattern: allowlist tool names + validate args. Please don’t ship any examples that eval arbitrary JSON into execution.

Sabrina James: +1. I’ll add an allowlist snippet in each language. Something like:

```python
ALLOWED_TOOLS = {"get_weather": get_weather}
...
if call.name not in ALLOWED_TOOLS:
    raise ValueError("tool not allowed")
args = json.loads(call.arguments)
validate(args)
```

Brian Murphy: One more: the partial args issue. Streamed tool args can arrive as deltas, so examples must aggregate until the tool call is “complete” (or until final response). Otherwise users try to `json.loads` mid-stream and blow up.

Ibrahim Khan: Yep, canonical flow should be:
1) accumulate tool call args by `tool_call_id`
2) only parse JSON once we have the full args string (on completed signal or end-of-stream)
3) validate against schema
4) execute tool
5) send tool result back and continue

Amara Diallo: + please don’t promise a “completed” event exists in all SDKs; some wrappers only give deltas + a final message. The doc should describe completion as “when the stream ends / when the SDK indicates the response is finalized.”

Henry Cho: Also parallel tools: examples should show multiple tool calls in one turn + rate limiting / concurrency guardrails.

Dana Lo: I can add a TS example that uses a concurrency limit (like p-limit) rather than `Promise.all` blasting everything.

Monica Patel: Decision recorded:
- Canonical term: “tool calling”
- Canonical location: redwood-examples repo
- Docs/SDKs should link back; avoid divergent copies

Action items:
- Ibrahim: add naming + event model section to canonical patterns doc, link PM-612 for product approval
- Sabrina: seed redwood-examples folder structure + consistent filenames
- Dana/Mateusz: update SDK README wording once canonical lands
- Elliot: prep docs redirect / glossary note (“function calling” -> “tool calling”)

:thumbsup: reactions from Dana Lo, Mateusz Zielinski, Elliot Price

Ibrahim Khan: I’ll also add a “Terminology” block we can paste everywhere:

“Tool calling: the model can request execution of developer-defined tools by returning structured tool call objects. You choose which tools are exposed and how to validate/execute them. Older docs may refer to this as function calling.”

Monica Patel: Perfect. Let’s keep it tight and consistent.

Sabrina James: I’ll open a PR in redwood-examples once I have the three flows (streaming, tools, structured output) aligned. Will post link here for review.

Elliot Price: Please tag me when it’s ready; I want to lift the exact snippets into the docs refresh PR.

Marcus Lin: + tag me for a quick safety pass before we ship.

Ibrahim Khan: Will do. Closing the loop here once the examples PR is up.
